hypothesis: The predeclared one-position-per-coin portfolio invariant reduces clustered same-symbol exposure when nearby signals repeat while an earlier lifecycle is still open, without requiring a new entry filter or cooldown.
decision: Retain one open position per coin and the four-coin shared portfolio ceiling. Do not pyramid, average, or open a duplicate same-symbol lifecycle from this evidence. Do not interpret the retained invariant as proof that the underlying entry signal has edge, and do not add a new cooldown or performance gate. In the frozen forward window, candidate paths classified prospectively as deployable were slightly positive while paths blocked by an existing same-symbol position were materially negative; the sample is too small and one-sided to estimate a durable economic effect, but it supports preserving the existing exposure-control invariant while more live evidence accumulates.
falsifier: Update this decision after a larger prospective, directionally balanced sample if existing-position candidate paths produce materially higher after-cost return than deployable paths and their opportunity benefit exceeds the avoided concentration and liquidation risk. Runtime evidence that two independent positions can exist for one coin, a portfolio classification made after observing the outcome, or a failure to reconcile candidate timestamps with the authoritative cohort snapshot would invalidate this revision.
limitations: Only eleven candidate paths are resolved; all are shorts and only HYPE and SOL are represented.

The candidate paths use recorded top-of-book executable estimates, an 80-bps stop proxy, a fixed 60-minute horizon, and measured fees and funding where available; they are not proof of actual IOC fills.
Candidate outcomes are non-additive and are not a reconstructed shared-account equity curve.
The apparent benefit is dominated by one blocked HYPE loss and two blocked SOL losses, so concentration and sign instability remain material.
The rule prevents duplicate same-symbol exposure; it does not validate the HYPE breakout entry mechanism on BTC, ETH, SOL, or HYPE.
The current open HYPE lifecycle is not treated as a resolved outcome, and no live position, order, stop, backend, profile, or execution authority changed.
Portfolio capacity did not bind in this window, so this revision evaluates the per-coin occupancy rule rather than the four-position ceiling.
